thread: maria_support: Hey team, customer ACME reports our OpenAI-compatible tool calling is failing for their integration.
maria_support_cont: They say the model returns a tool call but the args shape is an array instead of an object, so our schema validation throws and the tool never runs.
jon_engineering_1: Can you paste the raw response they saw?
maria_support_2:
Yep, pasted from their logs below. They hit our hosted API endpoint and forwarded the model's tool call payload.

```
{
  "name": "lookup_order",
  "arguments": ["{\"order_id\": \"1234\"}"]
}
```

So arguments is an array of a single JSON-string, not a straight object. They expect us to treat it as arguments obj and call the tool. We're rejecting it with 400: "tools.args.schema_mismatch".
jon_engineering_2: Ugh. We've seen two variants in the wild: 1) `arguments` as an object, 2) `arguments` as a JSON-string (stringified object). An array wrapper is new-ish. Could be a client SDK bug. Any repro steps?
maria_support_3:
Customer says they upgraded their OpenAI SDK to v0.25 and saw the change. They provided curl they used to call us (sanitized):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat/completions \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-XXX' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-4o","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"find order"}],"functions":[{"name":"lookup_order","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"order_id":{"type":"string"}}}}]}'
```
stella_qa_1: Quick thought: our OpenAI compatibility normalizer currently handles stringified JSON for `arguments` (we parse if it's a string) and accepts objects. We do not handle arrays wrapping the args. We should probably add a permissive path: if arguments is array and len==1 and element is string or object, unwrap it.
jon_engineering_3: Agree. Also need to check enums/field names: some models return `tool` vs `name`, or `arguments` vs `args`. We already normalize `tool`->`name` and `args`->`arguments`, but not this array case.
maria_support_4: Customer is blocked in prod, billing impact. Any quick mitigation we can apply at the gateway?
stella_qa_2: Test matrix: stringified in array, object in array, object direct, string direct, enum name mismatch (tool vs name). I'll add unit tests for each case plus an end-to-end harness hitting the API gateway with mocked model responses.
maria_support_5: Customer asked for ETA. Can we do a hotfix today?
jon_engineering_5: If infra team allows a minor runtime change we can push to canary within 2-3 hours. @infra_bot can you open the deploy window?
infra_bot: :gear: Deploy window requested by jon_engineering for runtime compat hotfix. Need approval from eng-sre. ETA estimate: 2h to staging, 4h to canary, 8h to prod after smoke checks.
maria_support_6: I'll tell the customer we aim for a canary fix in ~6 hours and will run them through the workaround in the meantime.
jon_engineering_6: Workaround for now: if they control the SDK, downgrade to previous SDK that produced object `arguments`, or have client-side patch before sending to us: replace `arguments: [x]` -> `arguments: typeof x === 'string' ? JSON.parse(x) : x`. Also we'll accept a request from them to attach the raw model response so we can repro.
maria_support_7: Customer provided raw model response and trace-id: trace-7a9. I'll upload to the ticket and link here. Thanks all — I'll update once canary is live.
jon_engineering_7: After ship, we should add telemetry: count occurrences of array-wrapped args so we can decide whether to make tolerant behavior permanent or add a strict flag. Also log model name + SDK version when available.
stella_qa_3: Added test checklist to the ticket. I'll run regression against function-calling flows to ensure we don't accidentally accept malformed payloads that could be an injection vector.
maria_support_8: :thumbsup: closing loop — will follow up with customer once canary rolled.
